# MCMC ergonomics and documentation {#sec-mcmc-ergonomics}

- The things that make fitting a model in greta pleasant rather than
  possible: methods for getting at what the sampler did, sensible
  defaults, progress reporting, and the documentation that explains
  how to fit and troubleshoot a model. Grouping labels: the `mcmc`
  cluster, `documentation`.
- This is the third piece of the old 34-issue sampling milestone. It
  depends on milestone 4 only where it touches the sampler interface;
  most of it can be written at any time.

**The shape of the work.** Three groups, loosely related.

The **accessors** - [#439](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/439)
(extract MCMC behaviour from a fitted model),
[#649](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/649) (a `thin()`
method), [#651](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/651)
(splitting `calculate()` into separate functions) and
[#731](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/731) (estimated time
to fit) - are all "greta knows this, but will not tell you" problems.
They want the sampler interface from milestone 4 to have settled on
field names first, or they will be written twice.

The **defaults**: [#294](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/294)
argues the default number of chains is far too low, and
[#413](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/413) that initial
values should be drawn from the priors for any inference, not just
some. Both change behaviour rather than adding capability, which is
what makes this milestone a minor release rather than a patch.

**Progress reporting** is one decision taken twice:
[#773](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/773) asks for the
progress bar to be abstracted, and
[#450](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/450) asks whether
`progressr` should be what sits behind it. Answer [#773](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/773) first; [#450](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/450) is
then an implementation choice rather than an open question.

The **documentation** issues - [#146](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/146), [#147](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/147), [#271](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/271), [#541](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/541), [#681](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/681), [#718](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/718) -
are independent of everything, including each other. They are the
natural filler for a patch release, and [#541](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/541) (a guide to fitting and
troubleshooting MCMC) is the one most likely to reduce the issue
tracker's own inflow.

- 2019-07-24

### [Issue #439](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/439)

- 2021-09-20
- Up Next
- Methods to extract MCMC behaviour (adaptation, step sizes) from a model.
- problem: sampler diagnostics are buried in the sampler object.
- finding: relates to the sampler-interface work (milestone 6) that names the boundary.
- fix: a read-only `mcmc_diagnostics(draws)` accessor on `greta_mcmc_list` that reads the fields the sampler already accumulates (`log_epsilon_bar`, `mean_accept_stat`, `diag_sd`, `numerical_rejections`, `accept_history`; `R/sampler_class.R:10-32`) via `get_model_info()` and returns a per-sampler data frame; re-point at the milestone-6 interface once it stabilises field names.
- **the proposed per-chain return shape is wrong — verified.** There is **one sampler object serving all chains**, not one per chain (`n samplers: 1`, `n_chains: 2`), so `lapply(info$samplers, ...)` yields a single element and the acceptance test's `expect_equal(nrow(as.data.frame(diag)), 2)` ("one row per chain") **will fail**. `mean_accept_stat` and `log_epsilon_bar` are scalars shared across chains; the only per-chain quantity is `accept_history` (iterations x chains). Rework the shape to "one row per **sampler**, per-chain values derived from `accept_history`".
- also pin the semantics before exposing anything: the raw `mean_accept_stat` reads **0.042** against an `accept_target` of 0.651, which is not a run-level acceptance rate — it looks like residual state from the final burst. Publishing it as `accept_rate` would have users conclude their sampler is broken. Prefer `colMeans(accept_history)`, which also gives the per-chain shape the issue asks for.
- context: convergence diagnostics are already covered via coda (`effectiveSize()`, `gelman.diag()`) and `posterior::summarise_draws()`. What is genuinely missing is **sampler/adaptation** behaviour, which today requires digging into an undocumented `model_info` attribute and an R6 internal. A public accessor is warranted.
- proposed fix: see [fixes/issue-439.md](fixes/issue-439.md).
- priority: medium.
- defect in the proposed fix: the acceptance test in `fixes/issue-439.md` does not run. It builds on `distribution(as_data(rnorm(10))) <- normal(mu, 1)`, which parses but fails at runtime with *"target of assignment expands to non-language object"* - a replacement function needs an assignable name on the left, so the test fails at model definition, before reaching the behaviour under test. Assign first: `y <- as_data(rnorm(10))`, then `distribution(y) <- normal(mu, 1)`.
- defect in the proposed fix: the per-chain return shape is wrong. There is **one sampler object serving all chains**, not one per chain, so `lapply(info$samplers, ...)` yields a single element and the acceptance test's `expect_equal(nrow(as.data.frame(diag)), 2)` ("one row per chain") **will fail**. `mean_accept_stat` and `log_epsilon_bar` are scalars shared across chains; the only per-chain quantity is `accept_history` (iterations x chains), so per-chain values must be *derived* from `colMeans(accept_history)`. Related: the raw `mean_accept_stat` reads 0.042 against an `accept_target` of 0.651 - it is not a run-level acceptance rate, and exposing it as one would have users conclude their sampler is broken.
